title: Plan under versions of the failure curves

expected.says: Run's report for the tiny fleet matches the expected report

blueprint.signature: def curve(kind: str, scenario: Scenario = BASE) -> tuple[float, float]
blueprint.contract: (beta, eta) of a kind's failure curve under a scenario: KINDS[kind].beta times scenario.beta, and KINDS[kind].eta times scenario.eta.
blueprint.idea: A scenario is a version of the model's data, here the curves every coefficient comes from.

lesson.title: 14.3.7 Uncertain Failure Curves: Scenarios and What Changes

blueprint.signature: def risk_removed(t: Transformer, start: int, request: Request, scenario: Scenario = BASE) -> float
blueprint.contract: As before, with both the old unit's and the new unit's PoF taken from the scenario's curve (pof_next and risk_table take the scenario too, with the base curves by default).
blueprint.idea: Under another curve the failures move, so every coefficient moves with them.

lesson.title: 14.3.7 Uncertain Failure Curves: Scenarios and What Changes

blueprint.signature: def evaluate(fleet: list[Transformer], request: Request, replace: dict[str, int], scenario: Scenario) -> float
blueprint.contract: What a finished plan removes if the scenario is how the fleet fails: the sum of risk_removed under the scenario over its replacements, $k.
blueprint.idea: Value a plan outside the model, so any plan can be scored under any scenario.

lesson.title: 14.3.7 Uncertain Failure Curves: Scenarios and What Changes

blueprint.signature: def build(fleet: list[Transformer], request: Request) -> Built
blueprint.contract: As before, with the objective over request.scenarios (the base curves alone when there are none): for objective "expected", the sum over scenarios of weight / total weight times that scenario's coefficients; for "worst", a continuous variable `worst` (0 to an upper bound you derive), a row `worst_<name>` per scenario keeping it at most what the plan removes under that scenario, and `worst` maximized.
blueprint.idea: A weighted mean of linear objectives is one linear objective; a max-min is a variable bounded by each scenario's objective, maximized.
